text: On 2024-09-18 the Fed cut rates by 50 basis points, to 4.75% to 5%. The vote was 11-1. Dissenting: Michelle W. Bowman. Key line: “The Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent, and judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.”

On 2008-12-16 the Fed cut rates by 75 basis points, to 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 10-0. Key line: “Since the Committee's last meeting, labor market conditions have deteriorated, and the available data indicate that consumer spending, business investment, and industrial production have declined.”

On 2022-06-15 the Fed raised rates by 75 basis points, to 1.5% to 1.75%. The vote was 10-1. Dissenting: Esther L. George. Key line: “Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures.”

On 2020-03-15 the Fed cut rates by 100 basis points, to 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Loretta J. Mester. Key line: “The coronavirus outbreak has harmed communities and disrupted economic activity in many countries, including the United States.”
On 2001-01-03 the Fed cut rates by 50 basis points, to 6%. Key line: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6 percent.”

On 2004-06-30 the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, to 1.25%. The vote was 12-0. Key line: “The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.”

On 2015-12-16 the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, to 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 10-0. Key line: “Given the economic outlook, and recognizing the time it takes for policy actions to affect future economic outcomes, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent.”

On 2019-07-31 the Fed cut rates by 25 basis points, to 2% to 2.25%. The vote was 8-2. Dissenting: Esther L. George, Eric S. Rosengren. Key line: “In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent.”
On 2023-07-26 the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, to 5.25% to 5.5%. The vote was 11-0. Key line: “Inflation remains elevated.”

On 2026-09-16 the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, to 3.75% to 4%. The vote was 12-0. Key line: “The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.”
On 2006-06-29 the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, to 5.25%. The vote was 10-0. Key line: “Readings on core inflation have been elevated in recent months.”

On 2007-09-18 the Fed cut rates by 50 basis points, to 4.75%. The vote was 10-0. Key line: “Today’s action is intended to help forestall some of the adverse effects on the broader economy that might otherwise arise from the disruptions in financial markets and to promote moderate growth over time.”

On 2025-12-10 the Fed cut rates by 25 basis points, to 3.5% to 3.75%. The vote was 9-3. Dissenting: Stephen I. Miran, Austan D. Goolsbee, Jeffrey R. Schmid. Key line: “The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.”
On 2026-10-28 the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4%. The vote was 10-2. Dissenting: Lisa D. Cook, Beth M. Hammack. Key line: “Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace.”

On 2011-08-09 the Fed held rates at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 7-3. Dissenting: Richard W. Fisher, Narayana Kocherlakota, Charles I. Plosser. Key line: “The Committee now expects a somewhat slower pace of recovery over coming quarters than it did at the time of the previous meeting and anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline only gradually toward levels that the Committee judges to be consistent with its dual mandate.”

On 2025-12-10 the Fed cut rates by 25 basis points, to 3.5% to 3.75%. The vote was 9-3. Dissenting: Stephen I. Miran, Austan D. Goolsbee, Jeffrey R. Schmid. Key line: “The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.”

On 2026-04-29 the Fed held rates at 3.5% to 3.75%. The vote was 8-4. Dissenting: Stephen I. Miran, Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, Lorie K. Logan. Key line: “Inflation is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices.”

On 2019-09-18 the Fed cut rates by 25 basis points, to 1.75% to 2%. The vote was 7-3. Dissenting: James Bullard, Esther L. George, Eric S. Rosengren. Key line: “Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports have weakened.”

On 2016-09-21 the Fed held rates at 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 7-3. Dissenting: Esther L. George, Loretta J. Mester, Eric Rosengren. Key line: “The Committee judges that the case for an increase in the federal funds rate has strengthened but decided, for the time being, to wait for further evidence of continued progress toward its objectives.”

On 2024-09-18 the Fed cut rates by 50 basis points, to 4.75% to 5%. The vote was 11-1. Dissenting: Michelle W. Bowman. Key line: “The Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent, and judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.”

If the rate on a $400,000 mortgage 30y moved +25 bp from 7.24%, the monthly payment would change by about $68.13 (from $2,725.99 to $2,794.12). 30-year mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate directly.

If the rate on a $5,000 credit card moved +50 bp from 21.19%, the monthly payment would change by about $2.08 (from $88.29 to $90.38). Card APRs are set off the prime rate, which moves with the fed funds rate.

If the rate on a $30,000 auto 60m moved +25 bp from 7.54%, the monthly payment would change by about $3.57 (from $601.71 to $605.28). Auto loan rates move partly with the Fed; fixed-rate loans you already have do not change.

If the rate on a $10,000 credit card moved -25 bp from 21.19%, the monthly payment would change by about $-2.08 (from $176.58 to $174.50). Card APRs are set off the prime rate, which moves with the fed funds rate.

If the rate on a $300,000 mortgage 30y moved +50 bp from 7.24%, the monthly payment would change by about $102.67 (from $2,044.49 to $2,147.16). 30-year mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate directly.
